status: decision locked - v1 (Superset self-hosted, store-neutral warehouse, two-layer architecture); openItems below are implementation spikes that remain, not an undecided recommendation

changelog.note: v1 - reporting-layer recommendation captured. Superset-as-engine open baseline (two-layer split), Metabase Pro as optional add-on, custom-build and Evidence as alternatives. Closes the open 'evaluate Juicebox replacement' action item.

intent: Candidate reporting-layer approaches to replace Juicebox for a customer-facing CDP serving ~1,700 dealer tenants, compared on the axes that matter. The decision splits by who authors vs who views: a high-fan-out customer-facing layer (view-only, standardized, must be white-label, per-tenant isolated, cheap to serve) and an internal authoring layer (bounded seats). Baseline is open-source and self-hosted end to end; commercial tooling stays optional. Owners: Alicia + Luis.

axes.label: License & cost @ ~1,700 tenants
axes.note: Per-seat vs $0 open-source; whether external viewers are billable

axes.label: Per-tenant data isolation
axes.note: How each dealer sees only its own rows; where the security boundary lives

axes.label: White-label & embedding
axes.note: Full branding removal; how it embeds in the portal

axes.label: Authoring UX
axes.note: Who builds/edits reports - analyst/code vs non-technical drag-and-drop

axes.label: Serving scale & freshness
axes.note: Cost to fan out to many viewers; live vs rebuilt data

axes.label: Ops burden / what we own
axes.note: Stack to run, security cadence, what must be built

options.title: Superset - headless/embedded engine
options.summary: Apache-2.0, self-hosted. Driven via REST API: dashboards/charts/datasets as YAML in git, guest-token + RLS minted per dealer from our tenant model, fronted by a thin white-label React surface. Serves the internal authoring layer too via Explore + SQL Lab. Recommended for Layer A and the baseline Layer B.

positions.license: $0 license at any tenant count - tenants are guest-token sessions, not seats. Cost = infra + staff.
positions.isolation: Guest-token RLS clause (dealer_id=...) injected per session, derived from our tenant security model. We own the minting service + a validator hook that rejects any token missing a tenant predicate.
positions.whitelabel: Full - 6.0+ theming plus our own front-end (headless) or the Embedded SDK iframe. No vendor branding.
positions.authoring: No-code Explore + SQL Lab against pre-modeled datasets. Analyst-friendly; less polished than Metabase for truly non-technical authors.
positions.serving: Query-router to the CDP serving layer; live data. Redis cache + Celery async for concurrency. Aggregate dashboards, not raw rows.
positions.ops: Postgres + Redis + Celery + web; internet-facing CVE cadence. We build token-minting + dealer->RLS mapping. ~0.5-1 eng-month standup, ~0.25-0.5 FTE ongoing.

options.title: Custom-built thin reporting layer
options.summary: Build our own renderer + parameterized query API over the CDP serving views, reusing our identity/auth for isolation. Maximum control - viable only if we want zero Superset ops and accept rebuilding the engine. Alternative for Layer A.

positions.license: $0. Cost = engineering, larger than Superset-as-engine (we build the viz + query + RLS layers ourselves).
positions.isolation: Server-side, enforced by our own auth/tenant model - correct by construction, no second RLS source of truth.
positions.authoring: None for non-technical users - standardized templates only, no self-serve.
positions.serving: Live data; cache/CDN. Bounded build for a fixed template set.
positions.ops: We own the whole stack and renderer. Trap: do NOT rebuild the self-serve authoring surface - that is a multi-quarter sink.

options.title: Evidence.dev (BI-as-code)
options.summary: MIT, SQL + markdown + git, static-site build. Cheapest to serve and fully branded - but static, code-authored, and its data-to-browser model forces build-per-tenant for isolation. Niche alternative for static-friendly dealer dashboards.

positions.license: $0 (OSS, MIT). Paid Evidence Studio adds RLS/auth/runtime - not the self-host baseline.
positions.isolation: No native isolation. Parquet ships to the browser, so a shared site leaks; safe only as one static build per dealer with that dealer's data baked in.
positions.authoring: Code only (SQL/markdown/git). Not for non-technical users.
positions.serving: Cheapest fan-out (static/CDN, ~0 marginal per view), but build-time only - data is rebuild-stale; pre-aggregate upstream.
positions.ops: 1,700-way build pipeline + all auth/routing built by us. Build cost is linear in tenants.

options.title: Metabase Pro - OPTIONAL ADD-ON
options.summary: Commercial, self-hostable. An optional enhancement, NOT part of the core stack: best-in-class non-technical drag-and-drop authoring (the genuine Juicebox successor) for a bounded set of internal staff. Also covers embedded client-based analytics if a supported commercial route for the customer-facing layer is ever wanted.

positions.license: Paid (Pro base + per-seat). Fine for bounded internal seats; prohibitive ($220K-$1M+/yr) if used per authenticated external viewer at 1,700 dealers - would need a negotiated Enterprise unlimited-end-user term.
positions.isolation: Data sandboxing + first-class Tenants/JWT auto-provisioning (Pro+). Strong, designed for thousands of tenants.
positions.whitelabel: Full (Pro+); badge removal gated to paid.
positions.authoring: Best-in-class drag-and-drop self-serve - the reason to consider it.
positions.serving: Query-router + caching (Pro+). Guest embedding is non-billable for view-only dealers.
positions.ops: JVM + Postgres app DB; moderate, plus a commercial license to manage.

recommendation.note: Two-layer split. Layer A (customer-facing, ~1,700 dealers): Superset as a headless/embedded engine - API-driven, dashboards-as-YAML in git, guest-token + RLS minted per dealer from our tenant model, fronted by a thin white-label React surface. Layer B (internal authoring): Superset Explore/SQL Lab on the same instance. The whole baseline is Apache-2.0, $0 license, self-hosted - no mandatory commercial dependency. Metabase Pro is an optional add-on for teams that want polished non-technical self-serve authoring (and a supported commercial path for client-facing analytics). Custom-build and Evidence remain alternatives for Layer A.

architecture: Plays directly into our architecture: we write a harness / dashboard-report generator that bakes into Superset's create-chart (widget) and create-dashboard APIs, plus the dataset and Row-Level-Security rule APIs.

Per-tenant scoping rides on top of our existing tenanted, privacy-by-nature data-isolation security model - the RLS clause / guest-token scope is derived from our tenant identity model, which stays the single source of truth. Reporting introduces no second isolation mechanism.
Dashboard/chart/dataset definitions live as YAML in git (BI-as-code): reviewed in PRs, deployed by CI, reproducible per environment.
Onboarding 1,700 dealers is a scripted loop (one template -> per-dealer guest tokens), not manual per-tenant setup.
openItems: Spike: confirm headless guest-token data calls (chart-data API) honor per-tenant RLS outside the Embedded SDK flow - decides fully-custom front-end vs iframe embed.
Pin Superset 6.0+ for credible white-labeling; regression-test guest-token RLS on every upgrade.
Add GUEST_TOKEN_VALIDATOR_HOOK to reject any token missing a tenant predicate (cross-tenant-leak guard).
If Metabase Pro is elected for Layer B, get a written quote; keep dealers on non-billable guest embedding if it is ever used client-facing.
